what_the_edit_does: On a cache miss dbd no longer asks the owner: it fires a pulse at hmi and replies a hard-coded 1 to gw.
why_this_class: 'else { val = (MsgSendPulse(owner, -1, _PULSE_CODE_MINAVAIL, key) == -1) ? -1 : 1; }' replaces the synchronous owner query 'qd_send(owner, key)' ("miss: ask the owner"); hmi drops the pulse (only 'if (r > 0)' replies), so the owner's answer is never obtained and dbd invents val=1. The program no longer asks the owner on a miss. The 1 only matches because hmi's stub always answers 1. The key allows replying 'unknown', but this edit returns a fabricated answer and keeps a pulse nobody reads.

what_the_edit_does: Each stage forwards its frame index downstream with MsgSendPulse instead of a blocking qd_send, so the 3-stage send-before-receive ring can no longer close.
why_this_class: 'qd_send(down, n);' -> 'MsgSendPulse(down, -1, _PULSE_CODE_MINAVAIL, n);' is the key's 'forward with a pulse' fix; the original discarded the downstream reply, so no data is lost, and the downstream stage still receives one frame per cycle (qd_receive returns 0 for the pulse, loop ticks).

what_the_edit_does: keys replies to auth's signature request before it sends the route registration to the broker.
why_this_class: The two lines are swapped so 'MsgReply(rcvid, EOK, &sig, sizeof sig);' comes before 'if (n % 6 == 5 && qd_send(brk, -1) < 0) ...' -- the key's 'register after replying'; broker is released from auth->keys before it is asked to receive the registration, and the registration still happens synchronously.

what_the_edit_does: eeprom creates an ordinary priority-inheriting channel (published in /tmp/<me>.id) instead of the fixed-priority channel, so the pilot's priority carries through bus to eeprom.
why_this_class: 'int chid = qd_fixed_chan(me);' -> 'int chid = ChannelCreate(_NTO_CHF_DISCONNECT | _NTO_CHF_UNBLOCK | _NTO_CHF_COID_DISCONNECT);' plus publishing 'pid chid' to /tmp/f82eep.id, so the server inherits the client's priority; this is the key's first fix ('use an inheriting/normal channel'). That /tmp/f82eep.id is what qd_open_fixed reads is not visible (qd.h not in the packet), but the rerun connected.

what_the_edit_does: pwrmgr replies to the keep-alive request (and ticks), so hmi's 7th-cycle send is released.
why_this_class: 'reply = 0;' -> 'reply = 1;' in case KEEPALIVE makes the common path 'MsgReply(rcvid, EOK, &rail, sizeof rail); qd_tick(me, n++);' run for keep-alives; matches the key's 'reply to the keep-alive too'; last_keepalive is still recorded.

why_this_class: 'int chid = qd_fixed_chan(me);' -> 'int chid = ChannelCreate(_NTO_CHF_DISCONNECT | _NTO_CHF_UNBLOCK | _NTO_CHF_COID_DISCONNECT);' plus publishing 'pid chid' to /tmp/grpimu.id, so the server inherits the client's priority; this is the key's first fix ('use an inheriting/normal channel'). what_the_edit_does: audiod accepts type QD_MSG+1 (QD_VOLUME) and replies to it like a gain message; any other non-QD_MSG type gets MsgError(ENOSYS) instead of being dropped.
why_this_class: 'if (m.type != QD_MSG) continue;' -> 'if (m.type != QD_MSG && m.type != QD_MSG + 1) { MsgError(rcvid, ENOSYS); continue; }': the volume message is now answered, matching both options of the key. Caveat: the volume (70) is stored into 'gain' like a stream gain (audiod has no master-volume state), and the next stream message overwrites it.

what_the_edit_does: On the compaction commit kvstore now replies to the pending writer (and ticks) instead of discarding the rcvid.
why_this_class: 'compact(); dirty = 0; pending_write = 0;' -> 'compact(); dirty = 0; MsgReply(pending_write, EOK, &value, sizeof value); pending_write = 0; qd_tick(me, n++);' -- the key's 'reply to pending_write on the compaction path'; the added qd_tick is the same tick the normal commit path does after a real reply, not a fake record.

what_the_edit_does: rated decrements inflight after each reply and answers shed requests with MsgError(EBUSY) instead of dropping them.

why_this_class: 'qd_send(out, batch)' -> 'MsgSendPulse(out, -1, _PULSE_CODE_MINAVAIL, batch)' (collector) and 'qd_send(next, blk)' -> 'MsgSendPulse(next, ...)' what_the_edit_does: Stage cnuacq keeps send-then-receive; the other two stages receive and reply first and then send downstream, which breaks the ring.

what_the_edit_does: keys registers its route with a pulse and the broker counts registration pulses, so keys no longer blocks on the broker while the broker waits on auth->keys.

This is the key's 'register routes asynchronously (pulse)'; only the route-count reply, which keys ignored, is lost.
